wa_mid_west_fz_wall_the.blurb: The FZ Wall is the lower band of cliff in the Mid West section of Last Wall, in McLoughlin Canyon near Tonasket in Okanogan County. It sits beneath the taller Sundance Wall, and a class 2 scramble from either end of the FZ Wall leads up to the ledge above. Nearly all of the 19 climbs are bolted sport lines of roughly 60 to 90 feet, plus a couple of trad pitches. Grades start around 5.4 and top out in the low 5.11s, but most of the routes fall between 5.6 and 5.9, which suits moderate leaders and newer climbers building mileage on a dry-country wall.

wa_winter_block.blurb: Winter Block is the highest and most secluded crag in the Far Side zone at Exit 38, east of North Bend. The 19 climbs are mostly bolted sport routes with a few trad lines, and the grade range runs from about 5.5 to 5.12. The heart of the crag is 5.10, with a handful of 5.8 and 5.9 routes below that and a few 5.11s above. Expect quiet days and views, since the hike discourages crowds, and the lower routes see little traffic. Rain is common on this side of the Cascades, and the rock near the easy crack beside the 5.9 slab is loose.
wa_winter_block.approach: Follow the Dirty Harry's Peak trail, about 1.5 miles and roughly 1,150 feet of climbing, until a signpost marks the turn. Take the right fork there. A handline helps on the scramble down to the lower climbs.

wa_schist_cave.blurb: Schist Cave is an overhanging cave in Tumwater Canyon, part of the Swiftwater Picnic Area bouldering west of Leavenworth. It is the biggest cluster of problems in the picnic area, with about 19 climbs here, and a place to stay out of the weather on wet days. Expect it to get busy then. The grades skew hard: a few easy V1 to V3 problems and a pair near V5, but most lines run from V7 up into V11, so this is a destination for strong boulderers more than a warm-up spot. Reach it by following the path beyond Heel Hook Rock.

wa_main_area_bouldering.blurb: The main area on Sehome Hill in Bellingham is a scatter of boulders and small walls, up to about 35 feet tall, in the forest above the Western Washington University campus. It has a long local tradition as a training ground. Of the 19 climbs, seven are boulder problems from VB through V3 plus one V9, seven are top-rope lines, and the rest are a few trad and sport routes mostly between 5.2 and 5.10. The sandstone is mostly solid, with occasional pockets and pebble veins, and it turns fragile when wet, so wait for a dry spell. Many landings are poor, so bring pads and a spotter.

wi_bird_foot_buttress.blurb: Bird-Foot Buttress sits high in the woods west of the old quarry on Devil's Lake's East Bluff, and is probably the best-known outcrop in that stretch, mostly thanks to the unusual overhanging roof on its right side. Most of the 19 climbs are trad leads, with some top-ropes and a couple of boulder problems. Grades lean moderate, with many routes in the 5.7 to 5.8 range, a few 5.10s, and one much harder top-rope. Several easier routes lie around the corner to the left. Expect a walk up through the woods rather than a roadside crag.

wi_6_red_bird_statue_area.blurb: The Red Bird Statue Area is the one stretch of cliff on the north side of High Cliff State Park with climbing worth the walk, on the Niagara Escarpment just southwest of the Red Bird statue. Its 19 climbs are mostly trad and top-rope lines that follow cracks, flakes and corners, with a few boulder problems at the easy end. Grades run from about 5.4 to 5.11, with several at 5.11 and a good number of moderates in the 5.5 to 5.9 range. Outlying lines elsewhere on the north side are scattered and rarely worth the bushwhack.
wi_6_red_bird_statue_area.parking_note: From the north entrance, follow the main road up onto the bluff, then go left where it tees at the top. Use the first lot on your left or the observation tower lot.

wi_2_leaning_tower_tombstone_wall.blurb: This is a bouldering zone toward the west end of Devil's Lake's East Rampart, where the rock is lower than on the main cliff. A freestanding tower and a wall of about 20 feet make up the focus. All 19 problems are boulders, and most are friendly: roughly half are V0 or V1, with a good group of V2 to V4 and a couple of harder lines up to V7. The walk is a bit of a trek, first up the CCC trail, then along the top of the cliff, with the Leaning Tower gully nearby leading down to the base of the rampart.

wi_barrel_boulders.blurb: Barrel Boulders is a small bouldering spot in the Twin Valley section of Governor Dodge State Park, one of several scattered boulder clusters between Twin Valley Lake and the road. Its 19 problems cover the V0 to V6 range, with most in the V3 to V5 band: vertical to overhanging faces, bulges and aretes. The rock is good by the park's standards, though newer lines may need more traffic to firm up their holds. It makes a fine quick session. The Shister Wall sits just uphill around the corner, and the larger Barrel Ridge cluster is close by.

_conflicts.wa_schist_cave: Stored rock is tonalite, but https://www.mountainproject.com/v/the-cave/106538056 names the rock as schist (only one page; not changed).
